title: Schubert’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User
entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.
notes: the pasted batch brief is summarised in brackets; the last sentence is verbatim

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Schubert’s Missing Symphony (work id schubert-symphony-1)

A four-movement symphony in A major, a key Schubert never used for a symphony. New music in his lyrical manner; no theme is taken from him, and it is not presented as a lost or completed Schubert work.

Orchestra (12 staves, sounding pitch): 2 flutes, 2 oboes, 2 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 horns and 2 trumpets (written as natural instruments in A; horns in F in the slow movement), timpani in A and E, strings. No trombones.

Movements
I. Allegro moderato, A major, 4/4. A song for the clarinet over murmuring strings, taken up by the violins and shaded with the minor. A dotted tutti ends on a bare E, and the second theme, for the cellos, enters a third below where it is expected, in C major; the closing theme regains E. In the reprise the same thing happens a fifth lower: the cello theme comes in F and the close in A. Exposition repeated.
II. Andante con moto, F major (again a third below the home key), 2/4: a walking song, its second strain shadowed by F minor; a stormy D minor episode with a lyrical B flat answer; varied return.
III. Scherzo: Allegro vivace, A major, with a sudden drop into C major, and a ländler Trio in D for the clarinet.
IV. Finale: Allegro vivace, 2/4: a sonata-rondo in constant motion, with a singing second theme for the woodwind.

Target length about fifteen minutes. Stylistic approach: long song-like themes, keys related by thirds, major–minor shading on a single note (F sharp to F natural), accompaniment figures that keep going under the tune. Compromise known from the start: tunes, the chord of every bar and the forms are written by hand; a program scores each passage in one of three textures (a tune over quiet strings, a woodwind band, the full orchestra) and writes accompaniment figures, wind chords and natural brass parts from the chord plan.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text: Build m1: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. First movement. Fixes after the first build: 14 parallel octaves/fifths between first violins and bass removed (chord inversions under the minor-shaded bar of the theme, five melody notes in the dotted tutti and the storm), an accented C sharp against the seventh of the dominant softened, and the reprise of the closing group lowered an octave (it ran above the violins' range).
